In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of reirradiating the brain in patients with multiple metastases, and the use of this method in a large number of patients.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of reirradiated whole brain irradiation should be considered as part of the management of patients with multiple brain tumors.
the benefit of whole brain radiotherapy is limited in patients with poor performance status or shorter cranial progression-free interval.
the second course of re-irradiation is not indicated in patients with poor performance status, short interval to the first course of irradiation, multiple brain metastases and extracranial disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with lung cancer, KPS ≥ 60 and longer cranial PFI should be considered for second whole brain irradiation.
patients with good performance and a longer interval between the first and second courses of whole brain irradiations might have better outcomes.
patients with lung cancer who have a longer interval between courses and a better performance status might have better outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
re-irradiation of the brain is feasible and safe.
the benefit of whole brain radiation therapy in this population is not only limited to patients who have a single brain lesion.
